background_rationale: An economist by training who spent 22 years running McKesson businesses, from U.S. pharmaceutical and medical-surgical distribution to McKesson Europe, before serving as COO and then CEO.

notable.summary: McKesson, with two other distributors and Johnson & Johnson, finalized a $26 billion national opioid settlement, with McKesson paying $7.4 billion over time without admitting wrongdoing.
McKesson announced its intent to separate its Medical-Surgical Solutions segment into an independent company to focus on oncology and biopharma services.
McKesson agreed to sell an approximately 13% stake in Medical-Surgical Solutions to Apollo funds for $1.25 billion, calling it a key milestone toward a planned separation and IPO.
Tyler added the role of Chair of McKesson's board to his CEO duties.

personal_story.hook: Brian Tyler's first job was cleaning machines in his father's shop; he now runs McKesson.
personal_story.summary: Tyler was born in Oakland, California, and says his first job, working as a janitor and cleaning machines in his father's shop, taught him that every job matters. He studied economics at the University of California, Santa Cruz, graduating with high honors, then earned a master's and a PhD in economics at the University of Chicago, specializing in industrial organization and labor economics. After three years in health care consulting at Integral, Inc. in Cambridge, Massachusetts, he joined McKesson in 1997. Over 22 years he led most of its major businesses, including McKesson Europe, before becoming CEO in 2019.
